reason: The only available combination pairs the hose and pump, which seem useful for moving recovered water to the garden.
expectation: I expect a pumped water line or similar assembly, though it may still need connecting at the garden service port.

effect: The hose and pump form a return loop that splashes water into the reservoir before sending it back to the beds; it still needs connecting at the garden port.
reaction: The splash is a useful detail, though I’m curious how much aeration it provides.
reason: Connecting the loop to the garden service port is the only gameplay action offered and appears to complete the water return.
expectation: I expect the loop to connect the treated moisture outlet to the garden reservoirs, though the exact connection is unclear.

effect: The connection completed the moisture return: treated condensate passes through a nutrient doser, and both beds drain back through the aerating loop.
reaction: It is satisfying to see water from the window return to the garden, though I would have liked more detail about how the nutrient dosing works.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the loop made the water cycle clear: treated condensate feeds the beds, which drain back into the reservoir.

leastWorthwhile.text: Assembling the loop was a fairly predictable first step because it was the only combination offered.

surprise.text: The return loop splashes water above the reservoir surface, adding an aeration detail I had not expected.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary, though the exact connections were unclear until the final result.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the practical water cycle was interesting, and I am curious how the garden develops.
